subject: Request: Trial sprint supplement + short-term discount to cover SLA gap
messages:
From: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@latticeworks.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — urgent: credits + short extension request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the onboarding help this week. We ran a higher-than-expected set of adversarial tests as part of the sprint and burned through most of the trial quota. Two things that matter to us right now:

- We experienced intermittent latency misses on two high-priority flows that slowed validation; product needs a few more runs to be confident.
- Our procurement cycle is still in legal/CFO review, so we need runway to finish the eval before a purchase order.

Can Redwood provide a short supplement of credits (~$12k equivalent) and a two-week trial extension, plus a temporary SLA concession while we finish validation? If you can also confirm a short formal amendment or MoA we can sign, that would help legal.

Kevin (cc) is on standby for any billing/legal confirmation. Appreciate a quick reply — we want to avoid a rollout delay.

Best,
Elaine Kim
Head of Product, LatticeWorks

[Attachment: sprint_usage_report.csv]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: finance_ops@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: FW: LatticeWorks — request for credits + 2-week extension (exec approval needed)

Team — please see the ask from LatticeWorks (external). Quick summary:

- Requested: $12k credit equivalent and a 2-week trial extension to finish validation.
- Reason: heavier-than-expected test run and legal/CFO still finalizing PO.
- Impact: high-touch enterprise account; strong forward pipeline (expected $120k ARR first-year).

Proposal I recommend:
1) Approve an immediate $8k credit to unblock the sprint and grant a 10 business-day extension.
2) Offer a conditional additional $4k credit contingent on a signed MoA or PO within 21 days.
3) Attach a one-page Amendment/MoA — legal can review the standard short-form we use for trials.

Pros: keeps momentum, reduces churn risk, predictable upside. Cons: short-term revenue concession and need legal sign-off for the conditional credit.

Attached usage report and a draft MoA (pilot_moa_draft.pdf). Can we get exec signoff on the $8k upfront + conditional $4k? Marissa/aditya — thoughts?

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pilot_moa_draft.pdf]

On Tue, Sep 28, 2027 at 10:03 AM PDT, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Team — please see the ask from LatticeWorks...

Soojin — I support the proposal with one adjustment. Approve the $8k immediate credit and the 14-calendar-day extension (to give them a weekend buffer). The remaining $4k should be structured as an invoice credit that posts once we have either:

- a signed MoA (preferred), or
- a legally-signed PO from LatticeWorks, or
- evidence of purchase commitment (salesforce/hubspot record + finance acknowledgement).

Legal — please review the attached MoA and provide any minimal edits. Finance — prepare a conditional credit memo template that we can email to Kevin/CFO once they sign.

I want us to keep this tight: 21-day window for the conditional credit to be claimed, otherwise it expires. Sergio — if you can operationalize the credit and update the HubSpot deal/notes, go ahead. After that, Soojin, send the confirmation to the customer with the attached Amendment and the conditional credit language.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
